Senses.PreferredTarget: before your parents gave birth to you

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Chan records turn the time before one’s birth into a pointed interview location from which a person’s original face, identity, or decisive word is demanded.
EvidenceBody: Xueyan Zuqin asks what it ultimately is before one’s parents gave birth. An identified lay questioner surnamed Wan turns his surname into a challenge about what he was called before that time. A verse attributed to Huineng answers with ‘originally not a single thing,’ while Tianyin Yuanxiu reports the phrase as a question repeatedly assigned for investigation.

Other records keep the answers concrete and discordant: an unnamed monastic asks for the original face, Yushan Shangsi pairs before-birth with a stone mortar fried in oil and after-birth with a steelyard weight dipped in snow, and Zhe’an Jingfan says that recognizing the person in a crowd also reveals this original face. These witnesses support the recurring temporal challenge without promoting any one answer into its definition.
